claims.text: Formation and crystal-structure selection in noble metal–based high-entropy alloy nanoparticles is governed by competition between rapid kinetic trapping of a metastable FCC phase and slower diffusion-driven phase separation.
Rapid heating and quenching lock in a uniform single-phase structure.
Extended dwell times permit diffusion-mediated elemental segregation.
Equiatomic Au-Ag-Pt-Pd-Rh nanoparticle precursors are initially well mixed and metastable, with minimal atomic segregation.
The target crystal structure for the equiatomic Au-Ag-Pt-Pd-Rh composition is FCC.
The controlled intervention uses heating at 50–100 °C/s to 500–600 °C, dwell times from sub-second pulses to more than 60 seconds, and rapid quenching.
The applicable compositional window has weakly exothermic mixing enthalpy.
Localized diffusion during the dwell, together with differences in mixing enthalpy and atomic size, mediates competition between homogeneous FCC formation and segregation.
Rapid thermal processing induces nucleation of a metastable FCC structure through kinetic trapping.
A sufficiently short dwell limits diffusion and preserves a homogeneous single-phase state.
Longer dwell times or slower heating increase atomic mobility.
Increased atomic mobility causes elemental clustering, phase separation, and non-uniform particle morphology.
Relative to rapidly heated and quenched samples, longer-dwell or slower-heated samples will show elemental clustering and diffraction evidence of phase separation.
Longer dwell periods will produce a distinct increase in diffusion signals and the onset of localized ordering.
The proposed mechanism applies to equiatomic or nearly equiatomic compositions processed at 500–600 °C.
Outside the stated composition and temperature boundaries, thermal decomposition, sintering, or other morphology instabilities may dominate.
A lack of increased diffusion signals and phase separation after extended dwell, with retention of the baseline uniform FCC phase, would falsify the proposed dwell-driven segregation mechanism.

contradictions.description: The conditions specify weakly exothermic mixing, which generally favors mixing, while the mechanism asserts that additional diffusion drives phase separation. Pair-specific thermodynamic or kinetic justification reconciling these statements is not supplied.

The prediction invokes slower heating as a cause of segregation, but the stated intervention and falsification experiment hold rapid heating fixed and vary dwell time, so the slower-heating prediction is not tested by the defined experiment.
